children: Gautam Adani announced the investment plan while laying the foundation stone for a 2,000-bed hospital in New Town near Kolkata

Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani on Thursday said the conglomerate plans to invest more than Rs 1 lakh crore in West Bengal by 2035, with investments planned across ports, logistics, power, roads and data centres.

The announcement was made after Adani and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari laid the foundation stone for a 2,000-bed hospital in New Town near Kolkata. The proposed Adani Arogya Mandir is expected to involve an investment of more than Rs 4,000 crore and include a medical college and research facilities.

Half of the hospital's planned 2,000 beds will be reserved for economically weaker sections eligible under state and central government health insurance schemes, according to the project announcement. The facility is also expected to create more than 10,000 jobs, the group said.
The wider investment plan covers infrastructure sectors including ports, logistics, power generation, transmission and distribution, roads and bridges, green cement and hyperscale data centres.

Adhikari said the state government was working with the Adani Group on industrial and healthcare projects. He said he had earlier requested Adani to invest in West Bengal and had also sought support for the revival of the state's industrial sector.

The chief minister said the proposed hospital would have capacity for medical education and research in addition to healthcare services. He also said the project could support medical tourism from northeastern states and neighbouring countries.
The hospital project is currently at the foundation stage and is not yet operational.
